The Doom Slayer skin comes after a wave of recent similar collaborations, with everything from Halo, Resident Evil, and Tomb Raider skins making appearances in Ubisoft’s FPS. “Doom means so much to me personally, and for many on the team that played Doom as kids growing up,” states Game Director Chris Budgens. “I think that skins are the best way [to implement most collaborations]. With skins, we get a lot more leeway in terms of having fun with the characters and franchises.

It has been revealed that to date, Rainbow Six Siege has only one permanent canon playable operator from a different fictional universe — Metal Gear Solid’s Solid Snake — and as The Doom Slayer joins as a skin, it appears that Ubisoft Montreal wants to keep it that way for now. “We don't want to just flood the game with different partners,” reflects Budgens. “It has to be right.”.

Industry observers note that snake’s inclusion, it seems, has been well judged. Since Solid Snake’s surprise introduction to Siege in March 2026, he’s become a beloved character in the game, slotting into Siege’s more grounded fictional universe with surprising ease. As I sit backstage at the Osaka 2026 majors, Ubisoft Montreal tells me that Solid Snake’s inclusion was an IP infiltration years in the making. “We had originally brought up the idea, and [Konami] were interested right from the get-go,” reveals Budgens. “One of the funny things was, what does this actually look like? Are we going with a skin? We had some interest in bringing Solid Snake as the operator into the game, but we had never really done that before—an operator from another franchise.”.

According to recent reports, creative director Joshua Mills, however, needed a bit more convincing that Snake would work in Siege’s gritty, grounded universe. “Alex Karpazis, the previous creative director, brought the idea to me and noted, 'Listen, I want to bring [Snake] into the game, and I was like, 'You want to do what? How's that going to work?'” recalls Mills, “'If you say the cardboard box, I'm walking away right now!”.

In a recent development, in order to make Snake work alongside Sam Fisher and alongside SWAT team-esque operators, they decided to reimagine Snake as a Tom Clancy-esque agent. “We came up with a very clear rationale, which was: it's Solid Snake as if he existed within the Rainbow Six universe,” recalls Mills. “It allows us to take everything that's iconic about the character and make it more grounded and canon in Rainbow Six…. Then we got to make that legendary pairing with Snake and Zero [Sam Fisher], an opportunity of a lifetime to be able to do that.”.

In a recent development, where the Doom Slayer is very much a classic skin-based collaboration, Mills suggests that The Boss’ inclusion in Rainbow Six Siege has opened the door to future fully fledged third-party operators. “We've definitely talked about other collaborations for a canon-based operator,” teases Mills. "We're very, very strict about who we would work with on this and who we would bring in because, again, we have to rationalise it one way or another. You can't just take any IP character and throw them in because it just doesn't work. That's where skin collaborations work fine… [but for operators ] There are some ideas, but nothing to confirm at the moment.".

Sources indicate that right now, memory chips are at all-time high prices for manufacturers, and that cost has been passed onto the consumer via increased prices of RAM sticks, smartphones, laptops, game consoles like the PS5, Xbox Series X, and Nintendo Switch 2, and just about anything that has memory in it. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The latest Google Health app update was supposed to bring a slew of performance improvements for some of the best fitness trackers, but instead, it unleashed a bug that's been plaguing Fitbit owners for the past few days.

According to the slew of reports on Reddit, a number of basic health metrics have gone missing from the view in the mobile app on both Android and iOS, including overnight vitals such as resting heart rate, blood oxygen, skin temperature, and HRV. Google rolled out its 5.12 upgrade last week, which appears to be the common link between user reports online.

According to recent reports, the bug isn't limited to just one device either — users on the fresh Fitbit Air and Fitbit Edge models, the Fitbit Charge 6, and Fitbit Sense 2 are all experiencing this absence. These vitals are tracked daily to establish patterns and highlight changes in your health, so if they miss a day or two, it could have a huge impact on your readings.

In a recent development, but despite these health metrics vanishing from thin air, it doesn't necessarily mean that your device has stopped tracking your data altogether. In some user cases, the device has continued monitoring health patterns, but the app has just failed to display them.

Still, it's not ideal, and customers have been quick to jump on Google's case — but the company has issued some reassurance that it's looking into it.

Among the wave of reports on Reddit, one user went the extra mile and reached out to Google directly, sharing the email they received in response: 'it's a joke' they shared.

Other customers turned to Google's support forum for answers, where one of Google's product experts mentioned they had escalated the matter.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

However, the issues in the app are persisting, and Google has yet to find a solution, leaving users to find their own workarounds for the time being.

One method you can try is simply logging out of the Google Health app and logging back in again. Some customers have found this helpful, but it hasn't been the golden ticket for others. In that case, try uninstalling the Google Health app altogether and redownloading it, which is a bit of a pain, but it's worth a shot.

We've reached out to Google for comment on the status of the glitch.

  • Sources indicate that A pre-Finals panel revealed that in Season 4, the largely forgotten healing character will be getting a huge revamp.
  • According to recent reports, it turns out, it's a good time to be a support player, because the Doc isn't the only healer-focused patch coming next season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you tuned in to the Rainbow Six Siege Osaka majors this weekend, you’ll have noticed that a long-sidelined operator took center stage — Doc. As 20 teams duked it out in front of a screaming crowd, competing to earn $200,000 in prize money, the trophy they were coveting was shaped in the likeness of the healer-focused operator. As palpable tension rippled through the packed ATC hall, moments before the tournament’s final, we soon discovered why.

Sources indicate that A pre-Finals panel revealed that in Season 4, the largely forgotten healing character will be getting a huge revamp. Instead of shooting direct stim pistol darts from afar, Doc will now be armed with a brand new gadget — the E-HEAL Monitor system. Using the E-HEAL, Doc will be able to remotely heal and — even revive — teammates from across the map (including through walls).

According to recent reports, it turns out, it's a good time to be a support player, because the Doc isn't the only healer-focused patch coming next season. Operator Thunderbird is also coming back in a massive way, with her Kóna Stations receiving a significant buff. Her number of Kóna Stations will be increased from 3 to 4 for broader site coverage, and if that wasn't enough to make you consider her, she’ll receive a latest weapon too: the MBZ-19. Thunderbirds really are go.

Alongside these intriguing operator remasters, an FPS legend is joining the fray — the Doom Slayer. In this surprise collaboration with Doom, the iconic anti-hero will become a part of Siege on December 22 in skin form — and you can read more about that here.

The beloved map Bank has also had an upgrade that seeks to level the playing field between attackers and defenders. Adding a fresh access point and exterior cover around the entry point, Ubisoft Montreal claims they're aiming to rebalance a map that's currently weighted too heavily in the defenders' favour. A new temporary testing ground will also allow the community to weigh in on a potential new secondary gadget which allows defenders to reinforce just part of a wall, leaving the rest open for lines of sight.

In a recent development, yet for hardcore fans, some of the most welcome changes will be the least exciting on paper. For year 11 and season 4, Rainbow Six Siege's UI has undergone a drastic overhaul, and with it, upcoming types of matchmaking have been introduced.

The Ranked ecosystem is getting an overhaul, splitting the competitive mode into dedicated Ranked Solo/Duo and Ranked Flex playlists. The aim is to keep individual and duo players from clashing with larger, coordinated squads, hopefully saving some frustration and heartache for solo players. This will work in conjunction with Cross-Queue Matchmaking, in a bid to keep those match queue times fast. Additionally, the level requirement to unlock Ranked will be dropping from 50 to 30, helping newer players to jump in sooner.

“The solo/duo ranked playlist is something that we've been trying to do for years,” beams Rainbow Six Siege Game Director Chris Budgens, "We've always gotten cold feet, so we started looking at how we actually pull off a solo queue within Siege, while respecting healthy queue times and so on. Every time we tried to do it, we would get scared by the data — this might be a bit more destructive than we're ready to deal with at the moment because we had other known quantities such as Rank 3.0 we wanted to work on.”.

According to recent reports, “We had so much data support in terms of our analysts and simulations and matchmaking queue times, and finally cracked it,” he adds. “We're really happy to be able to bring that to players because they've been asking for years to have a solo queue playlist.”.

Alongside new ranking queues, playing with your friends promises to be markedly less of a pain in the backside. An all-new Social Hub consolidates Ubisoft Connect and first-party platform friends into a single list, aiming to offer cleaner and less intrusive notifications. Players will now be able to invite friends to games via a single code, letting you generate a squad code to share on social media, negating the need to search for them on Ubisoft Connect.

Alongside the new invite system, the store’s been overhauled, aiming to provide clearer — and easier — browsing. Celebration packs will be making a return via the Winter Daily Rewards. Out of every 20 Winter Daily Rewards, five will be celebration packs. There’s now also finally a way to open multiple packs at once, letting players tear into multiple Alpha/Event packs at once to swiftly clear out their pack log. While not a reveal that will get fans pumping the air in excitement, it all adds up to a smoother play experience, which is a welcome change in our book.

Sources indicate that all in all, Season 4 looks to add a series of welcome — but not groundbreaking — improvements to Rainbow Six Siege. Yet while Season 4 so far may lack the excitement of a Solid Snake announcement, it points to a wider confidence in Siege — careful iteration rather than a table-up ending, solidifying the game's foundations before any potentially misguided attempts at innovation.

“One of the core vision steps we're looking at is protecting and focusing on excellence across the game in a lot of different ways — improving all the different things we do,” reflects Creative Director Joshua athan Mills on Season 4 and Ubisoft Montreal’s vision for continuing to shape Siege, “Whether that be anti-cheat, serviceability, or all sorts of things like this, we want to hone it and perfect it because 10 years in, Siege knows what it is, and it's crucial to listen to it and drive that forward.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • InfoQ Homepage News Netflix Turns Operational Data Into a Knowledge Graph for AI-Driven Observability.
  • Nov 13, 2026 3 min read.
  • Netflix is developing an ontology-driven knowledge graph to accelerate production investigations and provide AI agents with a shared understanding of its operational environment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

InfoQ Homepage News Netflix Turns Operational Data Into a Knowledge Graph for AI-Driven Observability.

Nov 13, 2026 3 min read.

Netflix is developing an ontology-driven knowledge graph to accelerate production investigations and provide AI agents with a shared understanding of its operational environment. The platform connects information about applications, incidents, deployments, alerts, and infrastructure dependencies, addressing a problem that can leave engineers spending hours piecing together information scattered across different systems.

According to recent reports, the firm claims it handles more than 2 billion requests daily and upwards of 38 million real-time logging events every second. During the November 2024 Jake Paul-Mike Tyson fight, its infrastructure supported approximately 65 million concurrent streams. Yet investigating a typical application regression can take around four hours, with much of that time spent reconstructing relationships between systems rather than analysing the underlying data.

Netflix's solution is to make those relationships explicit through an operational ontology and knowledge graph, creating a foundation for automated root-cause analysis and, eventually, self-healing infrastructure.

In a recent development, netflix already collects metrics, events, logs, and traces (MELT) across its applications and infrastructure. However, these signals are spread across systems such as alerting, incident management, deployment tooling, and engineering communication platforms.

It has been revealed that an application regression might originate from a client release, an experiment, infrastructure load shedding, or a service several dependencies downstream. Although each system contains useful information, engineers must often connect the evidence manually.

Netflix identified the missing capability as a consistent way to describe not just individual components, but how they relate to one another.

Recent findings suggest that its Observability Ontology provides that common model, defining operational entities, their properties, and the relationships between them. It uses established standards including RDF, OWL, SHACL, and SPARQL, while the resulting knowledge graph is stored in QuipuDB, Netflix's distributed RDF database built on Rust's redb storage engine.

The graph is populated through a pipeline of components Netflix calls enrichers. These consume information from operational systems and transform it into structured relationships, represented as subject-predicate-object triples.

Some enrichment is deterministic, while other stages use LLMs and probabilistic techniques to interpret less structured information. Netflix constrains these outputs through strict validation rules, including consistent entity types, URI naming conventions, and checks against its software catalogue.

Netflix also captures information from incident discussions, including hypotheses, rejected explanations, and mitigation decisions. This allows human reasoning to become part of the operational knowledge base rather than disappearing when an incident conversation ends.

Its correlation engine examines 13 types of signals, including log errors, metric anomalies, traces, alerts, incidents, deployments, configuration changes, experiments, and code changes. It searches for potential causal relationships, evaluating evidence such as temporal proximity and severity to produce ranked hypotheses.

It has been revealed that netflix describes the process as a knowledge flywheel: Observe, Enrich, Infer, and Adapt. As investigations produce newly introduced insights, those relationships can inform future detection and analysis. The knowledge graph also underpins AutoRCA, Netflix's internal agentic AI system for root-cause analysis.

In a recent development, rather than having specialist agents exchange loosely structured findings, they use the ontology as a common interface. Agents analysing traces, logs or deployments can contribute information about the same operational entities without needing to understand each other's internal implementations.

Netflix intends to use this foundation to produce ranked, evidence-backed explanations for incidents, with humans retaining approval authority over proposed changes and remediation.

In a recent development, platforms such as Datadog, Dynatrace, and Splunk already correlate observability signals and increasingly incorporate AI into incident investigation. Netflix's approach emphasizes the semantic model behind those signals, making operational relationships persistent and directly accessible to both engineers and machines.

Sources indicate that the firm ultimately wants to extend this capability from automated root-cause analysis into automated remediation and self-healing infrastructure. It also aims to explore integration with its Unified Data Architecture, connecting operational information to broader business and technology domains.

Sources indicate that most of us are probably familiar with generative AI. It’s what models like Claude and ChatGPT are basically about. You enter a prompt, and the AI responds. It’s more reactive and less proactive. However, agentic AI is becoming the next trend in the space, and it looks like Google’s Gemini task automation covers quite a number of apps on Android.

Instead, Google’s support page only mentions “select apps.” They also say that it supports “everyday tasks,” which includes booking flights and accommodations, buying tickets, and buying and selling products. Not particularly helpful.

However, thanks to Android Authority, they found a hidden server-side target app list on Android 17 that suggests that there are at least 134 apps that can take advantage of Gemini task automation.

Industry observers note that this includes apps that are region-specific. For instance, there are apps specific to Australia and Canada that made the list. This includes McDonald’s, KFC, Starbucks, Best Buy, Burger King, and 7-Eleven. It also appears that the target app list goes beyond the categories Google previously mentioned.

It covers productivity apps too, like Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams, OneNote, Slack, and Evernote. However, it’s worth noting that an app being on the list doesn’t automatically mean support for task automations. As Android Authority notes, apps need to be on the target list, but at the same time, Gemini needs to support the task you’re asking for.

All of this is to suggest that Google is laying down the groundwork for future updates to Gemini’s capabilities.

  • Chief among the problems that need to be addressed is the headlining massive unmonitored pool of roughly 26 million spare parts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Pentagon is struggling to track an astonishing 26 million F-35 warfighter parts, worth an estimated $31 billion, according to analysis published by the Government Accountability Office (GAO) this week. In its report — published just weeks after China purportedly swiped a classified shipment of F-35 parts diverted through Hong Kong — the GAO criticized the current inventory system as “outdated, inaccurate, and incomplete.” Possible solutions were also provided by the GAO; however, the implications are that the most advanced and costly fighter jets in U.S. history may not be ready and reliable due to inventory management deficiencies.

Inventory problems have been a long-standing feature of the deployment of the F-35, notes the source. The F-35 program is estimated to cost $1.9 trillion over its lifecycle. It is the most costly weapon system in history, indicates the GAO. But the Department of Defense (DOD) has “long-standing and ongoing deficiencies related to the accountability and financial reporting of F-35 parts,” asserts the watchdog.

Chief among the problems that need to be addressed is the headlining massive unmonitored pool of roughly 26 million spare parts. These are spread among 700 government and contractor facilities worldwide, but the technology for managing massive inventories has existed for decades.

According to recent reports, we might have seen a telling symptom of the inadequate F-35 parts tracking system back in September. A communications and/or accountability breakdown resulted in a UPS worker routing top-secret parts through Hong Kong to save time. They were allegedly swiped by China after an employee is thought to have missed an email warning not to divert the parts.

According to recent reports, frustratingly, this is the third report since 2019 from the GAO, and the latest published report complains that the DOD has “made minimal progress” in implementing past recommendations. For example, in a 2022 report, periodic physical inventories of F-35 parts were recommended but have not been implemented yet, notes Stars and Stripes. There is also no reliable procedure for verifying data from prime contractors, which can be “inaccurate and incomplete.”.

Recent findings suggest that presently, it is believed that there are over 1 million parts, worth more than $85 million, that are lost or missing. Moreover, about 17,000 parts that have been sent in for repair, worth as much as $42.5 billion, aren’t tracked.

It has been revealed that stars and Stripes mentions that the Pentagon is working on “a live connection” for the F-35 Joint Program Office (JPO), bridging its inventory software and that of prime contractors with F-35 parts. The JPO asserts that it is now modernizing its infrastructure with direct real-time interfaces. “This integration directly addresses previous system gaps to ensure seamless accountability of F-35 spare parts,” said a JPO spokesperson, quoted by Breaking Defense.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Databricks published an enterprise adoption overview on November 13, 2026, describing three ways to use OpenAI tools with governed firm data: ChatGPT analytics through Genie, centrally controlled Codex deployments, and custom agents hosted as Databricks Apps.
  • The guide builds on a multi-year partnership announced on September 25, 2025.
  • Under the joint architecture, OpenAI supplies GPT models, ChatGPT, Codex and its Agents SDK.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Databricks published an enterprise adoption overview on November 13, 2026, describing three ways to use OpenAI tools with governed firm data: ChatGPT analytics through Genie, centrally controlled Codex deployments, and custom agents hosted as Databricks Apps.

The guide builds on a multi-year partnership announced on September 25, 2025. The original release valued it at $100 million and noted native OpenAI models would be available to more than 20,000 Databricks customers across clouds. OpenAI co-founder and president Greg Brockman described AI without manufacturer data this way: “it’s like hiring someone with 20 PhDs and never inviting them to a meeting.”.

Under the joint architecture, OpenAI supplies GPT models, ChatGPT, Codex and its Agents SDK. Databricks contributes the lakehouse, which stores governed company data, along with business definitions, access rules, model-request routing and application infrastructure. Genie Ontology adds company-specific context.

Recent findings suggest that the business-user path targets employees who need figures but do not write SQL database queries. Through the Databricks Genie plugin, a ChatGPT user can ask a question in natural language; Genie identifies relevant data, applies approved metric definitions, runs the query in Databricks and returns graphs or charts. Genie Ontology records metrics, business definitions and relationships among organization data, so a metric such as revenue follows the company’s own definition.

Access remains limited to data the user already has permission to see, and each answer links to its Databricks sources. ChatGPT Work can also recommend next steps and who should be involved, share findings through Slack or email, and carry out user-approved actions through connected tools.

In a recent development, openAI’s plugin listing also covers SQL generation, summaries of dashboards or Genie outputs, and packaging findings for teams. Availability depends on the plugin, subscription plan and workspace settings, and some connections require administrator setup or approval.

Recent findings suggest that for engineering teams, Codex sends requests through Unity Gateway instead of contacting OpenAI directly. Developers retain their existing workflow and authenticate with a Databricks credential, while the OpenAI API key stays in the gateway. Every request is logged, and engineering leaders can set team budgets, review spending by team and choose which GPT model handles each task.

The recommended setup installs the Unity Gateway command-line tool and runs ug codex. Databricks’ setup documentation also covers manual configuration and running Codex on Databricks compute. Eligible ChatGPT Go, Plus, Pro and Enterprise subscriptions can connect through an administrator-configured model-provider service, with requests billed against the ChatGPT subscription. Unity Gateway itself is generally available; the documented SQL, sandbox and web-search tools and Unity Gateway skills remain in beta.

Sources indicate that the third path concerns custom agents for business processes that use data under strict security and governance rules. Databricks Model Serving runs OpenAI models beside that governed data, and no external API key is needed when Databricks serves the model. Teams can build and evaluate agents in Agent Bricks or use the OpenAI Agents SDK and deploy the result as a Databricks App.

The official app template supplies a conversational REST API, an interactive chat interface and MLflow evaluation code. Its MLflow AgentServer manages request routing, logging and error handling, with built-in tracing and observability. A ResponsesAgent interface provides compatibility with Databricks evaluation and deployment tools, while the Model Context Protocol connects the agent to tools and data sources.

Industry observers note that across these patterns, Unity Catalog supplies permissions, Unity Gateway handles request routing and cost controls, and Lakebase provides managed Postgres storage for agent memory and state. Databricks intends follow-up posts covering architecture, setup and customer lessons for each pattern.

That shared architecture gives business queries, coding requests and custom agents one permission and cost-control framework, making governance a common foundation as OpenAI use expands across a company.

The Lenovo Legion Tab Gen 5 would be my perfect Steam tablet if it didn’t cost $900

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, for every Android-powered slate I’ve used, only Nvidia’s Shield Tablet really stands out in my memory.
  • Industry observers note that even if Nvidia hadn’t abandoned the hardware game at the end of the last decade, it’s found new and much more destructive ways to make piles of cash at the expense of your easy access to RAM.
  • Sources indicate that but expectations around mobile experiences have come a long way since 2016.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, for every Android-powered slate I’ve used, only Nvidia’s Shield Tablet really stands out in my memory. Part of the company’s occasional (and all-but-dead) dip into hardware products, the Shield Tablet — and its revitalized K1 follow-up, which I also owned through a recall program on the original — carried me through the back half of college, frequently keeping my Chromebook in my backpack in lieu of a mini Bluetooth keyboard or the Shield Tablet’s built-in stylus. Its front-firing speakers made it great for movie-watching, and while I’m not much of a mobile gamer, I did find it to be a great device for emulation, especially when paired with an external controller.

Industry observers note that even if Nvidia hadn’t abandoned the hardware game at the end of the last decade, it’s found new and much more destructive ways to make piles of cash at the expense of your easy access to RAM. And considering the market for Android tablets in general, it’s not all too surprising to see very few companies trying to make headway into offering a miniature, gaming-focused tablet that can easily be thrown in a backpack. Lenovo, however, has managed to fill its spot quite well. 9to5Google’s own Ben Schoon found himself smitten with the Gen 3 model nearly two years ago, and now, its Gen 5 successor has found its way into my nostalgic hands.

Sources indicate that but expectations around mobile experiences have come a long way since 2016. Whether the Legion Tab Gen 5 can win over your heart really depends on your patience with some old-school Android jank — and whether your wallet can withstand an exceptionally-high asking price. Still, with recent advancements in PC emulation, it’s hard to say Lenovo isn’t onto something.

Considering the decade between their respective releases, I’m actually quite surprised just how much this tablet reminds me of the original Shield Tablet. Its 8.8-inch 16:10 LCD panel combined with a boxy matte-black design and a near-identical weight meant that I immediately felt at home holding this thing in my hands. You lose out on a couple of clutch features — most notably the built-in stylus — but largely speaking, this feels like the correct size and shape for a miniature gaming tablet.

Still, it’s not all perfect. Take, for example, the completely unnecessary camera bump that prevents this slate from properly laying flat on a desk. No one is buying this thing to use the camera, and judging by my very limited experience trying it out, I’m fairly confident whatever potato sensor is shoved in here would fit fine flush with the chassis. I’m pretty fed up with OEMs leaning on camera bumps to make any device look or feel more premium than it actually is, and that goes double quadruple for tablets like this.

Just like its predecessor, this thing still picks up smudges and fingerprints at an unreasonable level, its matte-black finish unable to hide anything. 360 grams is also a little heavier than I’d expect for a slate of this size, though to be fair, it’s much more noticeable in portrait than landscape. Holding the tablet with two hands to watch a movie or make my way through another round of Balatro made its top-heaviness much less noticeable.

Recent findings suggest that this display is sharp and fast — with one minor caveat — and reasonably bright in all circumstances except direct sunlight thanks to its 600 nits of brightness (and 800 in HBM). Really, it’s the LCD of it all that gets me here; this thing is nearly $1,000, and the lack of OLED alone makes it difficult to recommend at this price. It’s not an outright bad panel, but I found its contrast levels to be pretty lacking, with most blacks only ever showing up as dark grays on-screen.

In a recent development, oh, and that caveat: On two different occasions, I caught the tablet stuck in 60Hz mode, regardless of what refresh rate option I selected in settings. Switching back and forth between modes a few times eventually unstuck it, but it’s definitely a bug worth being aware of.

In a recent development, I think I’d feel a lot better about recommending this to someone looking for a content consumption device if this screen looked a little more premium. Your mileage may vary though — if you can get your hands on a demo unit before buying one, if only to see the display, I’d recommend it. For everyone else, this price tag might have you waiting for the OLED panel rumored to be arriving on next year’s successor.

At $900 — or potentially more, considering this tablet actually debuted at $850 — the Legion Tablet’s hardware leaves something to be desired. Biometrics are the most obvious weak spot; camera-based face unlock is the only biometric option provided here, without a fingerprint scanner in sight. I wouldn’t blame some if they saw this as a dealbreaker, because even if you’re willing to put up with the security concerns that a basic front-facing camera brings to the table, I can promise you you’ll be typing the code in all the time. Whether you’re trying to unlock in a darker environment or it’s just been four hours since you last unlocked the slate, make sure you have your pin memorized.

Industry observers note that if you’re primarily buying this as a content consumption machine, I think you’ll mostly have a great time. Lenovo built stereo sound into this slate, but did so in one of the smartest ways I’ve ever seen, ensuring all speakers are located to the right side along the bottom and top of the device. This might sound a little unbalanced in portrait mode, but in landscape, it guarantees you’re never actually covering up the speakers while holding the slate in your hands, something practically every other equivalent tablet is guilty of. No headphone jack here, unfortunately, something I would’ve liked to have seen on a gaming-focused device.

I find battery life genuinely difficult to judge on tablets, especially if you don’t pick it up every single hour of every single day, but I’ve been impressed overall with the Legion Tab’s longevity. Some weekend YouTube binge watching sessions at relatively high brightness settings left me with plenty of juice in the tank, and its standby time between sessions has been excellent. Obviously, if you’re really pushing your graphical limits on this thing — or if you’re emulating non-native software through something like DroidDeck — you’re going to see a bit of a dip, but combined with fast charging and two USB-C ports for both portrait and landscape access, battery life gets a big thumbs-up from me.

It has been revealed that lenovo’s packed a couple of accessories in the box with this thing, but I wouldn’t get too excited. While it’s nice to see a 68W charger included for those aforementioned fast top-offs, the included folio case is just awful. Not only does the triangle-shaped flap barely stick together to form a proper stand, but one of the corners of my case was loose enough to frequently flex back and forth. Holding the tablet while wrapped in its case just felt bad, in the way that so many bundled cases often feel, and a quick look at Amazon highlights that basically no recognizable brand — or unrecognizable, for that matter — has stepped up to offer something better.

The Legion Tablet also includes a screen protector in the box, if that’s how you roll.

Unsurprisingly, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 in here can handle effectively anything you dare to throw at it. While my mobile games might be limited to more casual, indie fare like Balatro — and, by the by, if you’re still enjoying Balatro a couple of years later, the size and shape of this device makes it perfect — graphically-intense games played fine. Asphalt Legends or the HoYoverse games might not be my cup of tea, but they perform excellently on this device, and compared to the 12-inch tablets companies like Samsung and Amazon have become obsessed with, the display size here actually feels perfect.

Industry observers note that we definitely have to talk about emulation, though, because it’s increasingly becoming the main focus of mobile gamers everywhere, and this feels like a tablet perfectly designed for something like DroidDeck. Getting Steam emulation — complete with the Deck’s usual Major Picture mode UI — available as an application on the Legion Tab Gen 5 takes all of two minutes and a handful of taps on your display, and I have to say, I’m pretty shocked at just how impressive the overall experience is right now.

DroidDeck gave me the option to bring my mini gaming tablet experience full-circle. While my Steam library has no shortage of games I think could run without stressing this slate, I wanted to push the envelope a little bit. Persona 3 Reload felt like as good a candidate as any: a modern title that doesn’t necessarily require quick response times and fits virtual controls quite nicely. Plus, most of my gaming time on Nvidia’s tablet a decade ago was spent working through Persona 3 Portable; like poetry, it rhymes. I installed the game, ran it on the Legion Tab, and to my surprise and delight, it was absolutely in a playable state.

Industry observers note that now, there are some caveats here. I did drop the game’s graphics preset to low, and even still, there were some occasional hiccups while running around an early dungeon. The game’s initial intros and disclaimers actually gave the impression the title wouldn’t run at all, but I was able to sneak up on a shadow, use a slash attack to begin the battle — basically the only thing in P3R that remotely requires accurate timing — and concern commands to my player character and party mates.

Sources indicate that obviously, your experience emulating Steam titles on the Legion Tab will vary on what you want to play, and with such wide variables between experiences, I probably wouldn’t push most gamers to run out and pick one up right away. It might be early days for DroidDeck, but considering how we’ve already seen it progress, I wouldn’t be surprised to see some buyers picking this up as a Valve-esque take on a gaming tablet.

With all of that power under the hood, though, it’s Lenovo’s take on Android that leaves a lot to be desired. It’s not just that this feels like a rough-and-ready take on AOSP, an unrefined package that would feel more in line with devices from a decade ago, though, yes, that’s half the struggle here. But at its worst, the Legion Tab Gen 5 simply feels unoptimized in daily use.

Sources indicate that scrolling through web pages or various apps often felt sluggish and heavy, like the UI elements on screen never actually match the movement of my finger, and it’s unclear how much of that was due to the refresh rate bug I described above. Auto-rotate was both super finnicky and super sluggish, alternating back and forth between one state or the other, and the auto-rotate button that pops up when it’s disabled would frequently fail to appear. Occasionally, I’d run into app problems, such as choppy playback on a 1440p YouTube video that got so bad — regardless of what resolution I selected — that I had to fully force close the app in settings to fix it. Even getting the slate to reliably wake up (or not wake up) when picking it up was annoying, as it’s simultaneously sensitive enough to frequently turn on when I don’t want it to, or to stay asleep when I’m trying to unlock it. Inevitably, I turned that setting off.

It has been revealed that you might think that shelling out $900 for an Android tablet would buy you an out from pre-installed bloatware; you’d be wrong. During setup, the Legion Tab attempts to install a whole host of apps and games, including Perplexity, TikTok, Temu, several match-three games that I’ve truly never heard of, and no less than two mahjong and solitaire titles each. In fact, there might actually be three solitaire titles depending on what “Jigsawcard Solitaire Puzzle” is, but I unchecked all of these apps during setup and didn’t deem the title worthy of bothering to check.

It has been revealed that while Lenovo has been trying to improve its software update policies on some recent devices, this slate isn’t among that group. To my knowledge, there is no official update schedule for this device, but based on past performance, I’d expect somewhere around 2 OS upgrades and 4 years of security patches, give or take.

According to recent reports, I would’ve loved nothing more than to recommend this year’s Legion Tab to small tablet fans and gamers everywhere, but when this thing is $200 more than Apple’s latest iPad Mini — which in and of itself is absolutely overpriced — and $100 more than the base OLED Steam Deck post-price hike, I just have a hard time telling anyone to buy it. Really, its Steam performance was one of the few areas that made me feel truly excited by this thing, but it’s simply too unpredictable an experience at this point (and price) for me to recommend.

Even setting aside the price, there’s simply too much here that feels unfinished or rough around the edges for my liking. A handful of bug fixes and a couple of additional optimization passes could fix a lot of my more minor quibbles, but despite what I just said, you can only ignore the $900 price tag for so long before it bites you in the ass.

We have seen a post-iPad Mini discount bringing this slate to an Apple-matching $700 ahead of the holidays, but even that price is $150 more than its predecessor was at launch without a whole lot to show for it. If you’re looking for a gamer-friendly tiny tablet, I do think Legion is a brand worth keeping your eye on, especially as DroidDeck and other Steam emulation apps continue to evolve. But at this point — and for this price — your best bet is waiting for whatever model follows this one. It might still be stupid expensive, but at least you’ll be getting OLED.

In a recent development, A decade ago, Nvidia’s Shield Tablet felt like a no-brainer addition to my everyday carry. But in this economy, gamers and tablet fans alike are simply better off dropping $900 elsewhere.

Recent findings suggest that google has released a fix for Google Health that restores missing health metrics and fitness data for affected iOS users. The upgrade, version 5.12.2, addresses missing readings, including heart rate variability, blood oxygen, and skin temperature.

Industry observers note that google Health is supposed to be the place where your health and fitness data is consolidated. It’s like a dashboard for all things health-related, so we can imagine how some users are annoyed that certain vitals and data were missing. Thankfully, Google has pushed out a Health fix.

According to Android Authority, Google has confirmed to the publication that it is rolling out a fix for the Google Health app that will address missing vitals and data. This comes on the heels of the release of version 5.12 last week.

The trouble started after version 5.12 landed last week. Fitbit owners reported missing heart rate variability, blood oxygen, and skin temperature readings. Resting heart rate and breathing rate vanished for some people too. One support thread opened on November 9 noted vitals had been missing for two to three days. Google states no data was lost. Version 5.12 also added blood pressure logging for Fitbit Air users.

In a recent development, in a statement shared with Android Authority, a Google spokesperson stated, “We are rolling out a fix for the glitch where a small number of iOS users were missing metrics like vitals and daily totals for steps, distance, and energy burned. Updating to app version 5.12.2 will fix the issue. No user data was lost.”.

Recent findings suggest that that being noted, if your vitals are still missing, here’s what you can do. For affected iPhone owners, they can check the App Store for version 5.12.2. You can also try signing out of Google Health and back in again. Some users say this brought the readings back. Some users also said switching to the weekly or monthly view helped.

It has been revealed that it’s worth mentioning that Google only mentioned iOS in its statement. So it’s unclear whether Android consumers saw the same bug. Most Android users are still on version 5.11 anyway, so they might be safe. Either way, it won’t hurt to double-check. If you do notice any missing vitals, you should probably report it to Google ASAP so they can work on a fix.

Google Open Sources Ambient Quality Agent (AQuA) to Diagnose Production AI Agent Failures

💡 Key Takeaways
  • InfoQ Homepage News Google Open Sources Ambient Quality Agent (AQuA) to Diagnose Production AI Agent Failures.
  • Nov 13, 2026 2 min read.
  • Google has open-sourced AQuA (Ambient Quality Agent), a reference implementation that analyzes production AI agent sessions, verifies recurring failure patterns, and investigates root causes against deployed source revisions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

InfoQ Homepage News Google Open Sources Ambient Quality Agent (AQuA) to Diagnose Production AI Agent Failures.

Nov 13, 2026 2 min read.

Google has open-sourced AQuA (Ambient Quality Agent), a reference implementation that analyzes production AI agent sessions, verifies recurring failure patterns, and investigates root causes against deployed source revisions. The tool targets silent quality regressions that conventional infrastructure monitoring can miss, such as agents ignoring user preferences or skipping required tool calls while returning successful responses.

AQuA runs alongside an agent in Google Cloud, outside its request path, reading telemetry from Cloud Trace, Cloud Logging, or BigQuery. It samples up to 1,000 recent sessions per run and processes them through five stages: sampling, reviewing, clustering findings, verifying candidate clusters, and tracking issues. Developers can configure domain-specific quality criteria through a goal.md file and add deterministic custom metrics. AQuA can run on a schedule, after a deployment, or on demand.

Industry observers note that for root cause analysis, AQuA compares failing sessions with an immutable source snapshot captured at deployment. Its diagnosis agent identifies relevant code or instructions, cites file and line ranges, and proposes changes when the cause lies in the repository. It can also attribute failures to external dependencies, tool handoffs, or retrieved data. AQuA does not apply fixes or open pull requests automatically.

AQuA sidecar architecture (Source: Google Developer Blog Post).

Google evaluated 32 sessions from a multi-agent travel application, identifying 42 findings grouped into nine candidate clusters. The verifier rejected three unsupported clusters after checking up to three full transcripts per candidate cluster, leaving six verified issues. Two involved bypassing seat availability checks and losing a traveler's vegan preference during delegation.

After developers modified prompts and replayed the sessions, seat-selection bypasses fell from 15 sessions to two, dietary-preference omissions dropped from seven to zero, and sessions passing all checks increased from five to 13. These results came from controlled replay, not production traffic.

An insight is its citations, not a self-reported confidence score.

Findings link to supporting traces, and proposed root causes must reference valid lines in the deployed snapshot. AQuA tracks findings as FRESH, RECURRING, or automatically RESOLVED after 14 days without being observed. Sampling can miss rare failures, and replay may not reproduce external state.

Reacting to the announcement on LinkedIn, Dmytro Aprelenko, engineering manager at Redcore, wrote,.

Agent orchestration definitely needs better continuous diagnosis to catch these loops early.

In a recent development, AQuA validates source references and links findings to supporting traces. Cluster verification filters false positives, though it cannot confirm every session exhibits the same failure. Google's Agent Platform evaluation service supports regression testing and production quality monitoring, while Arize Phoenix provides open-source tracing and evaluation. AQuA focuses on grouping production failures and linking verified findings to deployed source code.

Google identifies sampling limits and incomplete reproduction of external state as constraints. Its open-source implementation helps teams integrate production agent diagnosis into development and evaluation workflows.

Presented by: Kiran Gangadharappa - Engineering Advisor at Harness, and Scott Davis - Senior Engineering Manager at Harness.

Contractor turns a Milwaukee Hackzall into a portable Ethernet untwister after facing job requiring 50,000 custom Cat6 cables

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A contractor faced a project that required them to create 50,000 custom Cat6 cables from scratch, requiring 100,000 Cat6 terminations.
  • His first solution to the problem was to buy a “Wire Straightening Machine” from Alibaba for $500.
  • It worked well at first, but he soon discovered that it was too bulky to use in the tight and hard-to-reach places where Ethernet cables sometimes terminate, like when you’re installing this heavy-duty outdoor Wi-Fi 7 access point.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A contractor faced a project that required them to create 50,000 custom Cat6 cables from scratch, requiring 100,000 Cat6 terminations. The contractor, who goes by Analytical Horsepower on YouTube, had used a large, rare tool to streamline the job, but afterward he decided to build his own portable tool by modifying a Milwaukee Hackzall, cutting the time to straighten the twisted pairs to under two seconds.

His first solution to the problem was to buy a “Wire Straightening Machine” from Alibaba for $500. It does the job well enough, but it’s an industrial machine designed for tabletop use, requiring an AC power source for the power brick and compressed air to run. The concept is that it clamps the wire between two rubber grips using air pressure, and then a linkage converts the rotary motion of the motor into a linear one, allowing the grip to untwist the cable. Since he wanted to use the machine in the field, he needed to make the thing portable — so he disassembled the entire thing, replaced the DC power brick with a 20V DeWalt battery with an adapter, added a push-button switch for power control, and a portable bike pump to deliver compressed air on the go.

It worked well at first, but he soon discovered that it was too bulky to use in the tight and hard-to-reach places where Ethernet cables sometimes terminate, like when you’re installing this heavy-duty outdoor Wi-Fi 7 access point. So, he studied the concept — it involved two flat, grippy surfaces grabbing the twisted cables and then moving back and forth. The back-and-forth motion of the surfaces causes the cables to untwist, with the clamping force ensuring that it remains in contact with the cables as they become flatter.

Sources indicate that with this, he realized that he did not need such a bulky machine to do the job — he just needed a reciprocating tool that could accept a clamp. He first looked at a reciprocating saw, but he found that it still had the same bulky problem and also called it “not overly precise.” But when he looked at the Milwaukee Hackzall, he found that it offered the perfect balance of portability and precision. More importantly, it came with a detailed data sheet, instruction manual, and parts breakdown that allowed him to accurately 3D print the plastic parts and laser-cut and bend the metal parts he needed to build his machine. He also used a toggle clamp to hold the Cat6 cable in place instead of a pneumatic piston, which further simplified the machine and cut its size and weight.

After a few steps of trial and error, especially in the quality of the grippy materials used for the clamping surfaces, he finally got it to work. He could reliably untwist softer copper-clad aluminum cables in one go in under two seconds. Harder 100% pure copper conductors, sometimes called solid copper or pure bare copper Ethernet cables, must be untwisted pair-by-pair, though, requiring a bit more time, but it’s still undoubtedly much faster and more convenient than doing the job with just your bare hands.

Industry observers note that this tool isn’t worth it if you only untwist a few Ethernet cables every month or so, like this telephone-to-gigabit internet conversion job. But if you’re facing a massive job like Analytical Horsepower, that half a minute you save with every cable end could translate to over 830 cumulative hours of labor saved on the jobsite. It’s a great first-generation tool, with its practical use apparent in the YouTube video. Some commenters suggest extending the toggle clamp handle to reach the trigger so activating the tool is easier, while it also looks like a good idea if there’s a way to incorporate the entire system into a crimper.

#212. Tech Report: AI That Understands – Why Data Meaning Is the Key to Trustworthy and Explainable AI

Tech Report: AI That Understands – Why Data Meaning Is the Key to Trustworthy and Explainable AI

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Artificial Intelligence has made extraordinary progress in recent years.
  • Yet, as this power grows, so does its weaknesses, like hallucinations, hidden bias, lack of explainability, and governance challenges.
  • Every AI system, traditional or generative, is ultimately a consumer of data.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Artificial Intelligence has made extraordinary progress in recent years. From predictive models to generative systems capable of producing text, images, and code, AI has become one of the most powerful technological forces shaping organizations today.

Yet, as this power grows, so does its weaknesses, like hallucinations, hidden bias, lack of explainability, and governance challenges. The glitch is not simply how much data AI can process, but how well that data is understood.

Every AI system, traditional or generative, is ultimately a consumer of data. When data is ambiguous, inconsistent, or detached from its real meaning, even the most advanced models risk producing outputs that are statistically plausible but conceptually fragile.

This is where the conversation must shift, from models alone to meaning.

For years, organizations have rightly invested in becoming data-driven. Today, however, there is a growing and undeniable awareness that data alone is not enough.

Without a shared and formalized understanding of what data represents, information remains raw material without direction. Decisions are faster, but not necessarily wiser.

This marks the transition from a data-driven paradigm to a semantic-driven one, where meaning is not an afterthought but the very foundation of how data is accessed, interpreted, and used.

Recent findings suggest that this is precisely the role of Logical Data Architectures (LDA). Unlike traditional physical architectures focused on replication and consolidation, logical architectures focus on how data is conceptually organized, connected, and interpreted, independently of where it physically resides.

At the heart of a logical data architecture lies the semantic model.

It has been revealed that the semantic model is not just another technical layer. It is the grammar of knowledge: the place where data is tied to the concepts it represents, where relationships become meaningful connections, and where business rules are made explicit and verifiable.

It has been revealed that within the AI data layer, the semantic model acts as a bridge of meaning between heterogeneous systems, organizational domains, and perspectives. Rather than forcing uniformity, it harmonizes differences by providing a shared conceptual language.

This formalization of meaning allows organizations to:.

Recent findings suggest that AI does not truly “understand” data, it processes it. Meaning does not emerge automatically from algorithms; it must be explicitly embedded in the architecture that feeds them.

A well-designed semantic model provides AI with:.

According to recent reports, in this sense, the semantic model becomes a kind of structural conscience for AI. It does not replace algorithms, but it ensures that models know what they are operating on and why.

Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a response to the limitations of purely generative models, connecting Large Language Models to external knowledge sources.

It’s vital to point out that not all knowledge layers are created equal.

Industry observers note that without semantics, retrieval remains syntactic, and documents are selected because they contain similar words, not necessarily the right concepts. The result is often plausible – but unreliable – answers.

According to recent reports, with a semantic model, retrieval becomes conceptual. The system does not search for keywords, but for meaning, context, and intent.

In RAG architecture, the AI data layer acts as the semantic knowledge layer that translates natural language questions into conceptually grounded data access. This dramatically reduces hallucinations, improves contextual accuracy, and transforms probabilistic generation into context-aware reasoning.

Trustworthy AI is not AI that never fails, but AI that can explain its reasoning.

Semantic models enable what can be called operational ethics: not abstract principles, but observable behaviors grounded in transparency, coherence, and accountability.

Within our tech giant, governance naturally resides in the semantic layer, where security rules, access policies, and data masking are defined once at the level of meaning and then consistently enforced across all data sources and use cases.

This makes AI systems more governable, resilient, and sustainable, even as underlying technologies evolve.

According to recent reports, the relationship between Artificial Intelligence and semantics is not optional. It is the condition for moving from systems that merely compute to systems that truly understand.

A logical data architecture and semantic layer helps bridge this gap by connecting information across systems, establishing consistent definitions, and giving AI the context it needs to deliver more reliable insights.

As AI models become increasingly accessible, the technology itself will no longer be the primary competitive differentiator. The advantage will belong to organizations that can connect, understand, and act on their data faster and more effectively than their competitors. The future of AI will not be defined by who has the most data or the largest models, but by who can turn information into better decisions and measurable business outcomes.

Good morning. Today I’m finding open source alternatives to all of my apps, poring through Pitchfork’s list of the 100 best indie rock albums to find ones I haven’t listened to, and preparing my body for November 19th by pre-loading GTA VI (and replaying GTA IV in the meantime).

Inbox is written by Daniel Bader. Read previous complications here, and then catch up with Ben Schoon’s excellent Weekender column published every Sunday.

On Monday, I unboxed the iPhone Duo I pre-ordered back in October and experienced a disarming sense of déjà vu. It’s beautiful hardware married to a messy, often painful software onboarding experience atypical of Apple’s usual polish. It reminds me of the Galaxy Fold’s early years.

I was most looking forward to the combination of a foldable form factor and Apple’s superior app ecosystem, but even the apps that have been updated to support the new aspect ratio, on both the front and back, feel ungainly and buggy. In moving UI elements from the bottom to the right, even with the display open, the Duo forces a rebuilding of essential muscle memory that’s prevailed across mobile platforms, including Android foldables, for 20 years.

Sources indicate that the front display, in particular, is a massive test of one’s patience: apps, even ones ostensibly optimized for its stout dimensions, often feel unusable, with UI elements that would be prominent on the iPhone 18 Pro hidden behind overflow menus on the Duo. It’s exasperating and, frankly, boggling.

But what’s interesting is the enthusiasm with which developers are approaching the new form factor. Reddit threads reveal dozens of Duo-optimized app recommendations that feel novel and, if not polished, then propulsive. There’s a fascinating delta between waiting for my bank, or Starbucks, or Kobo, to get its act together to support the Duo and seeking out net-new opportunities and experiences.

I spent most of the summer using the Galaxy Z Fold 8, and I didn’t expect going back to it to feel so stately and predictable: the showcase of a platform with fewer highs but none of the Duo’s current lows.

According to recent reports, I’m not sure if I’m going to keep the Duo and wait out its colicky infancy. But I do know that until now I hadn’t given Samsung enough credit for the amount of work it did to make foldable software feel ordinary, and that’s the highest compliment I can pay.

This section has some of our favorite stuff from around the internet. Great videos, weird memes, fun reads, recommended apps, whatever. Send us your recommendations!

The $109 e-reader has a 4-inch screen, physical page-turn buttons, and an included magnetic case that can attach to a compatible phone. It competes directly with XTEINK’s excellent X4 Pro, which features a rudimentary touchscreen and backlight for around $100, though its magnets are built in.

It has been revealed that both products are wonderful examples of hardware companies adapting to the growing size and complexity of smartphones and seeing an opening for single-purpose products that do one thing really well. Plus, it’s fun to stick a thing to the back of your phone and… read it.

Sources indicate that for something you can explore without buying another device, Paolo Mainardi turned his personal website into a point-and-click adventure. Articles live in books, links sit on a notice board, and his about page is a letter in a lighthouse. The Context Island is an incredibly thoughtful and unique approach to “web” design, and it’s another example of how AI can really help bring crazy ideas to fruition.

In a recent development, langChain unveiled on November 13, 2026 that it raised $300 million in a Series C round at a $3 billion valuation. Existing investor CapitalG led the financing.

The capital backs LangChain’s work on LangSmith, a platform for operating, improving and governing agents regardless of the framework used to build them. Its stated mission centers on letting enterprises choose their models, control data and infrastructure, improve agents continuously and apply governance for secure operation at scale.

The round included significant participation from newly introduced investors GIC and DFJ Growth and existing investors IVP and Sapphire Ventures. Salesforce Ventures, Insight Venture Partners, QuantumLight and MongoDB Ventures also joined, while Sequoia, Amplify and Benchmark increased their participation.

LangChain expects agents built for specific domains to become standalone products and internal operational tools, differentiated by knowledge, data and user experience, with control of those systems forming the basis for lasting competitive advantage.

LangChain reports a LangSmith user base of more than 7,000 organizations. Its examples range from startups Harvey, Rippling and Listen Labs to Fortune 500 companies NVIDIA, Toyota and Salesforce. At Clay, the platform tracks hundreds of millions of agent runs each month and supports agent improvement. Workday uses LangSmith for organization-wide operation and governance, and cut the deployment time for a new agent from five months to under a day.

Those deployments illustrate why LangChain groups monitoring and governance with deployment: a high-volume agent operation needs visibility after launch, while a large organization also needs a shorter, controlled path into production.

LangSmith’s foundation is organized into Agent Runtime, Agent Improvement and Agent Governance. Agent Runtime covers the path from agent architecture to production infrastructure. Development teams use Deep Agents, LangGraph and LangChain to retain model choice and decide how context is managed. Secure, scaled deployment runs through LangSmith Agent Server and Sandboxes in either cloud or customer environments, while LangSmith Managed Agents and Fleet offer a fully managed route to production.

Agent Improvement pairs measurement with automated remediation. LangSmith Observability and Evaluation expose agent behavior and assess quality. LangChain states LangSmith Engine, its in-platform agent, looks for errors, produces code and prompt corrections, and checks production traffic for regressions. LangSmith Fine-Tuning helps teams convert agent traces into training data that can be used to tune and evaluate specialized models.

Recent findings suggest that the governance pillar centralizes control of models, tools and data. Teams can use the LLM and Tool Gateways to set model budgets and fallback behavior, safeguard sensitive information, and manage tool access and authentication across teams and agents.

LangChain has scheduled a release event for November 20, 2026, where it intends to share several additional LangSmith capabilities built on this foundation.

The central question for those releases is whether they make high-performing agents easier to build while preserving customers’ control over models, data, infrastructure and governance.

Apple says that Siri AI is an entirely new version of its assistant which is "profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal".

Today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, natural language, and more.

These new capabilities let users make natural language requests and have Siri AI carry out any custom action supported by the app. The framework also supports complex requests through Skills, a new feature that lets developers "teach Siri AI how to combine several actions into a single experience".

If a request does not specify an app name, it will automatically be routed to the app presently in the foreground, the app associated with an active Live Activity, or the app previously mentioned in the ongoing conversation. This allows people to continue conversations across an app and its Live Activity, or a different app altogether. While an app is running in the background, however, it will receive only requests that explicitly mention its name.

Requests can also include actions across apps, such as finding content in one app, sending it to another, and perform an action there.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the topic of U.S.
  • Industry observers note that the scientists are careful to hedge their findings, noting that while their math checks out, it does not reveal where the chips were, how they were accessed, or prove that export controls were broken.
  • This identification method is limited to models with open weights, and depends on both hardware and software stacks used for model training — and yet it's both clever and simple, like the Egg of Columbus.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the topic of U.S. trade controls precluding the export of Nvidia and AMD high-end AI accelerator chips to China has taken a few twists lately. Jensen Huang's affairs aside, it's an open secret in the industry that Nvidia's Blackwell silicon finds its way into China, whether physically or virtually. UnemploymentLabs, an independent research outfit, has come up with strong evidence that those chips were used for training open-weight Chinese AI models, including DeepSeek V4, Kimi K3.1, MiniMax-M3, and Ling-3.1-Flash.

Industry observers note that the scientists are careful to hedge their findings, noting that while their math checks out, it does not reveal where the chips were, how they were accessed, or prove that export controls were broken. As far as we can tell, it's presently not illegal for Chinese companies to rent Blackwell hardware abroad, and even though Nvidia's grip is tightening, U.S. companies aren't strictly prohibited from doing so, as evidenced by the recent Tencent-Oracle deal.

This identification method is limited to models with open weights, and depends on both hardware and software stacks used for model training — and yet it's both clever and simple, like the Egg of Columbus.

In a recent development, let's establish some base facts. First, different AI accelerator families have unique counts of shader modules (SMs), marginally analogous to CPU cores — Nvidia's Hopper chips have 132, Blackwell B series have 148, and Blackwell GBs come with 152. Second, while there's more than one software stack for training AI models, PyTorch and its CUDA-aware friends are by far the most widely used on the green team's hardware.

In a recent development, the first step for training a model is initializing its weights, or how strongly the model considers each individual input. In modern LLM architectures, their initialization goes through a randomization step in which their values are adjusted plus/minus pseudo-randomly, using cuRAND — as in, randomly, but a seed starting value results in the same adjustment figures every time.

Sources indicate that as you'd expect, doing this for an entire model is a lot of computational work, so this process is spread out across all the SMs, further subdivided into threads. For large weight sets, the thread count per SM is 2,048 for Blackwell and Hopper silicon, and it's surely carefully chosen and optimized for.

The researchers repeated a facsimile of the initialization process using the same chips, software, and thread counts. Using relatively simple statistical analysis, they spotted that their final statistical distribution of weight values precisely matched that of DeepSeek, Kimi, et al. As a test, they changed the SM and thread counts, and predictably, the correlation completely broke down.

Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

This let them pick out each family of Blackwell/Hopper chip used for each model, and eventually they also figured out an approximate count of cards used. They cannot, however, pinpoint which exact variation produced the weights, as this analysis is linked to initialization layout counts alone, thus SM count and usage pattern — not to VRAM capacity, memory bandwidth, or other characteristics that distinguish individual cards.

What about AMD cards like the MI300X, or other silicon with a high enough SM count, using the same software stack? The scientists say that it's not impossible that an AMD card could be set up to show up as two groups of 152 or 148 shaders, although we imagine there'd be little reason to do so. Nevertheless, for DeepSeek V4, they also ruled out that possibility by analyzing the actual weight values themselves, and found that AMD cards still didn't produce the same weight value pattern.

Google Maps offers turn-by-turn directions, while there’s real-time Google Translate in over 70 languages.
